newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to resume talks with London Club-agency.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to resume talks with London Club-agency.

text.p: Talks with the London Club of creditor banks on re-scheduling Yugoslavia's debts will resume in Belgrade on Wednesday and Thursday, the Yugoslav government was quoted as saying by the Tanjug news agency.
The Yugoslav proposal for the re-scheduling of debts is based on on the Yugoslav economy's realistic possibilities to fulfil its obligations towards its creditors, the government said in a statement.

"Additional information requested by commercial banks' representatives about the sources and dynamics of influx in and outflow of funds from the Yugoslav econony as the basis for the re-scheduling of obligations will be reviewed at the talks," the government said.
Yugoslavia asked in mid-June for debt forgiveness of 80 percent of its outstanding $2.4 billion debt and restructuring of the remaining $481 million through a 25 year syndicated loan facility.
Talks held in London on June 24 ended without result and analysts said the proposal was likely to be rejected.
